FACT_818.statement: The leaves become purple-brown when toxicity is severe

FACT_819.statement: Rice plants remain stunted with extremely limited tillering

FACT_820.statement: Causes reduced plant height and dry-matter accumulation

FACT_821.statement: Tiller formation and productivity can be severly reduced

FACT_822.statement: It is associated with fewer panicles per hill

FACT_823.statement: It can cause delayed flowering and maturity by up to 25 days or cause no flowering

FACT_824.statement: Can cause root growth to stop and roots break down and are coated with a dark brown to black precipitates

FACT_825.statement: Symptoms can be more pronounced in a dry as compared to a wet season crop

FACT_826.statement: Toxicity is generally linked to high-rainfall and humid areas

FACT_827.statement: Soil toxicity tends to be more at sites where the parent rock is rich in iron

FACT_828.statement: Attempt to intercept interflow of iron containing water from surrounding areas by either constructing irrigation or drainage canals, or with rows of other plants such as bananas

FACT_829.statement: Avoid adding large quantities of easily decomposable organic matter, particularly in clay and acid-sulfate soils

FACT_830.statement: Apply potassium fertilizers to limit microbial iron reduction in the rhizosphere

FACT_831.statement: Use flush irrigation rather than flood irrigation to reduce iron toxicity

FACT_832.statement: Delay flooding to reduce iron toxicity

FACT_833.statement: Use shortened submergence periods to reduce iron toxicity

FACT_834.statement: Drain the field mid-season to temporarily remove iron toxicity

FACT_835.statement: Consider using direct seeding rather than transplanting seedlings because root damage during transplanting can make plants more susceptible

FACT_836.statement: Ensure soil contains sufficient potassium to prevent iron toxicity, by either applying mineral potassium fertilizers, or if unavailable then use rice straw

FACT_837.statement: Zinc application increases rice tolerance to iron toxicity

FACT_838.statement: Depending on the soil and season, application of potassium, phosphorous, calcium, magnesium and zinc, solely or in combinations, can reduce bronzing symptoms and increase rice yield
